newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends lower, tracks Australian dollar slip.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends lower, tracks Australian dollar slip.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended lower on Thursday in line with a sharp fall in the Australian dollar, which lost half a U.S. cent on the back of worse-than-expected unemployment data, dealers said.
The Kiwi ended near its lows for the day at US$0.6908/18, down from 0.6932/39 at the opening. The Trade-Weighted Index (TWI) was also soft, closing at 68.71 from 68.84.
The Australian dollar, having hit a high for the day of US$0.7860, was ending locally US$0.7808/13.

"The Aussie really dragged it down," said one dealer. "But the interbank market has been short Kiwi for the last couple of days and this is an area where people have been taking some profits," he said.

"I think Aussie might come under pressure in the next 24 hours. That employment report will probably weigh on the Aussie and the Kiwi could probably test as low as 0.6900, but I don't think it's going to come back too far," he said.
Upside in the Kiwi was expected to be limited to around 0.6925-30.
There was confusion initially from wire service reports about Finance Minister Bill Birch's contact with ratings agency Standard and Poor's.
Dealers said they nevertheless took from them the message that the country faced a positive sovereign debt rating outlook.
